lines: "Serious question. How do you know any of this is real? How do you know we're not running inside something?"
"Because I'd have to be worth the electricity, and I'm not."
"That's the argument though. If you can run one world you can run a thousand, so the odds you're in the real one are terrible."
"That only works if somebody ever builds one. Nobody has. You're doing arithmetic on a number nobody's found yet."
"Everything underneath is numbers anyway. Ask a physicist."
"Describing a thing with math doesn't make the thing math. My rent's a number too. The room's still a room."
"It's real. You just want it to be somebody's fault."
